thread:
Maya R: Heads-up — Acme reported a sharp latency/503 surge around 10:45 UTC. They were pinned to na-west but we observed a lot of requests routed to eu-central and ap-northeast. Some of those fallbacks returned 401s. Ticket ACME-789. Sample req ids: r_aa12, r_bb34.

DevOps-bot: metric snapshot: na-west.queue_depth=525, spillover_count=410 (5m), default_route=capacity-first, fallback_targets=(eu-central, ap-northeast).
```
router[na-west] WARN queue_depth=525 trigger=spillover
router[na-west] INFO fallback initiated -> eu-central
auth-proxy ERROR validate_token: audience_mismatch -> 401
```

Jordan M: Quick repro steps I ran locally to mimic the hit:
1) k6 script sending 600 concurrent connections pinned to na-west
2) watch controlplane metrics `curl -s http://controlplane.internal/metrics?shard=na-west` -> queue climbs past 300
3) once queue > 400 router starts sending ~30% traffic to eu-central; those calls hit fallback path and returned 401s.
Command I used:
```
k6 run --vus 600 --duration 30s acme_spike.js
# simple POST to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with ACME_ORG_TOKEN
```

Alex C: Root cause summary: fallback path authenticates using the router's cluster SA (svc:router-default) which does NOT include the org-specific token audience/scope we recently introduced for Acme. Primary (pinned) path validates with the org token proxy and succeeds. Fallback path rejects -> 401. Also saw an exponential client retry pattern which multiplied token usage and caused a billing jump.

Tara P: Short-term mitigations to pick from:
- Disable auto-spillover for acme-org (pin them to na-west) -> prevents 401s but may keep them in a congested region (higher latency).
- Spin up 2-3 burst instances in na-west immediately.
- Create a temporary fallback token mapping so fallback routes present a fallback-compatible token (quick patch).
- Change route policy for acme-org to `latency-prefer` so we prefer local capacity even if throughput suffers.
Which should we do now?

Jordan M: I pushed a conservative plan: 1) pinned acme-org -> route_override id ro-3021 (spillover_enabled=false) rolled to 10% canary then 100% after smoke; 2) added 2 burst GPUs to na-west (nodes b-3001,b-3002). Both actions live.
Config snippet:
```
route_overrides:
  - org: acme-inc
    policy: latency-prefer
    spillover_enabled: false
    id: ro-3021
```

DevOps-bot: actions executed: added nodes b-3001,b-3002 to na-west pool; monitoring: alert if queue_depth>150 for 5m; canary ro-3021 -> 10% -> 100%. Billing tracker flagged: rate_limit_retries spiked.

Alex C: Longer-term fixes (postmortem items):
- auth-service: support token audience negotiation for fallback paths OR propagate org-token through fallback path (avoid swapping to cluster SA).
- Implement per-org fallback token mapping (secure short-lived fallback tokens).
- Update router logic: before cross-region fallback, attempt local short-term burst scaling + shed low-priority requests rather than immediate spill to region with incompatible auth.
- Add regression test: simulate heavy queue + token_audience mismatch in chaos runs.

Finance L: Billing impact recorded — created BIL-554 to reconcile the 3x charge during the incident window. Please attach retry logs.

sre-bot: incident created INC-2101 (owner: Jordan M). Postmortem assigned to Alex C. Follow-ups: CFG-3021 (route override), AUTH-99 (fallback token mapping), RR-104 (routing circuit change).

auth-service: note: logs show `validate_audience failed for token: expected=org:acme, got=cluster:router-default`. We'll propose a short-term token mapping API to bridge the gap.

Maya R: I'll notify the customer with what we changed (pin + extra capacity) and explain the 401 cause and billing spike. Once they confirm stability I'll close ACME-789. Also note: avoid `capacity-first` global default for orgs using org-scoped tokens; it's too risky without fallback token mapping.

Tara P: I'll write a 1-pager runbook for oncall: how to pin an org, add bursts, and roll route overrides. Will include quick commands and the exact controlplane endpoints. :thumbsup:

Jordan M: closing loop — traffic back to normal for Acme, queue_depth now ~30. Leaving incident open for auth-service changes and billing reconciliation.
